sections.html:
Monmouth County occupies the central coast of New Jersey, bordered by Middlesex and Mercer Counties to the west, Ocean County to the south, the Atlantic Ocean to the east and Raritan Bay to the north. Of 661.40 square miles, only 468.18 are land, because 29.2% of the area is water. Freehold Borough is the county seat, and the county holds fifty-three municipalities.

The shore towns, from Long Branch and Asbury Park down to Spring Lake, set the market for oceanfront homes, while western towns such as Freehold, Marlboro and Colts Neck are inland and more rural. Middletown Township is the most populous municipality, with 67,106 residents in 2020, and Howell Township is the largest by area at 61.21 square miles.

Municipal offices send the bills. Each of the county's towns has its own assessor and tax collector, and the Monmouth County Board of Taxation oversees assessments and hears appeals. The board sits at the Hall of Records, 1 East Main Street, Freehold, NJ 07728, and its phone number is (732) 431-7404.

  • Five members are appointed by the governor.
  • The board hears assessment disputes, and the municipality is represented by its attorney.
  • All of its meetings are public.

The county also offers a property tax estimator through its record search, which owners can use to project a bill.

For a payoff before closing, call the collector for the town where the house stands. Your title company will ask that town's tax office for the figure.

Monmouth follows an alternate assessment calendar, and the tax appeal deadline is January 15 rather than April 1. Burlington and Gloucester counties are on the same calendar. Hearings are generally held after the January 15 deadline, and the board generally denies adjournments.

What the board expects from you:

  • An assessment is presumed correct, so the owner must prove it is excessive or discriminatory.
  • Evidence should relate to the October 1 assessment date, and at least three comparable sales go to the assessor, the clerk and the tax board a week before the hearing if they were not filed with the petition.
  • All taxes and municipal charges through the first quarter must be paid to the collector.
  • Owners of income-producing property must supply an income statement on the board's forms.
  • A skipped hearing leads to dismissal for lack of prosecution.

A dissatisfied owner has 45 days from the mailing of the judgment to appeal to the Tax Court of New Jersey. If the assessment is over $1,000,000, the owner can file directly with the Tax Court by April 1. The Chapter 123 test also applies: when the ratio of assessment to true value exceeds the average ratio by more than 15%, the assessment is reduced to the common level.

Monmouth took part in an Assessment Demonstration Program created by P.L. 2013, c. 15, which moved the county toward more frequent reassessment. A university study found that inequity in residential assessments dropped after the program began, and the county's assessors association and tax board received a 2019 Distinguished Jurisdiction Award from the International Association of Assessing Officers.

For owners, values are updated more often, so a change in the assessment notice reflects recent sales instead of waiting for a one-time revaluation. Middletown's aggregate preliminary net value for tax year 2026 was 7.94% above 2025, and the rate was expected to fall as a result. You can look up property record cards, sales data and prior postcards in the county's online record search before deciding to appeal.

Monmouth is a wealthy, owner-heavy county, and with more than a fifth of residents over 65 it sees plenty of sales by longtime owners, heirs and downsizers.

Hurricane Sandy in 2012 hit the northern Jersey Shore hard, and whole neighborhoods in Monmouth County were demolished and rebuilt, some at a higher price level than before. For a seller, a location on the water or near a train line sets much of the price, and the assessor's record for your lot sets the tax.

The state offers relief that applies in every county. The fiscal year 2027 budget funds the Senior Freeze, ANCHOR and Stay NJ programs, each with a yearly application window, so check the Division of Taxation relief page for the next one. Local assessors handle the senior, disabled and veteran deductions on the municipal side, and many offices will also review a property record card with you.

A sale during the year may change eligibility, so ask the state program office how a mid-year move affects a claim before you close.

sections.h2: Selling in Monmouth County with a tax balance
sections.html: The collector in the town where the house stands issues the payoff, and the closing agent pays it from your proceeds. Ask for the figure in writing, with interest through the closing date. If you are mid-appeal, remember that all taxes and municipal charges through the first quarter have to stay current. A cash purchase skips the lender's steps, but the tax payoff and deed recording still happen the same way, so start the conversation with the collector early.

faqs.q: What is the Monmouth County property tax appeal deadline?
faqs.a: January 15. Monmouth uses an alternate assessment calendar, and the statewide April 1 date does not apply to most owners. An assessment over $1,000,000 can go directly to the Tax Court by April 1.

faqs.q: How do I contact the Monmouth County Board of Taxation?
faqs.a: Call (732) 431-7404 or write to the County Board of Taxation, Hall of Records, 1 East Main Street, Freehold, NJ 07728. The board can send the forms needed to file an assessment appeal.

faqs.q: What if I disagree with the Monmouth County Tax Board's decision?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date the judgment was mailed to file a further appeal with the Tax Court of New Jersey. Missing a hearing leads to dismissal for lack of prosecution, which can block that next step.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Monmouth County property tax bill itself?
faqs.a: No. Taxes come from local budgets and cannot be appealed. You can challenge only the assessment, and you must pay all taxes and municipal charges through the first quarter while the appeal is pending.

faqs.q: How many comparable sales do I need for a Monmouth County appeal?
faqs.a: Submit at least three comparable sales. The board wants them delivered to the assessor, the clerk and the tax board at least a week before the hearing if they were not attached to the petition.
